LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: SYMBOLS/CHARACTERS OF THE ALPHABET

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.2: Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you develop a good handwriting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. copy words and sentences accurately
2. appreciate the characters of the Arabic Alphabet

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING: SYMBOLS/CHARACTERS OF THE ALPHABET
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED WRITING: SYMBOLS/CHARACTERS OF THE ALPHABET
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Copy words and sentences accurately

What this means
In this part you learn to copy words and sentences accurately. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: copy words and sentences accurately.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can copy words and sentences accurately. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the characters of the Arabic Alphabet

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the characters of the Arabic Alphabet. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the characters of the Arabic Alphabet.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the characters of the Arabic Alphabet. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: copy words and sentences accurately)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet to a partner. (skill: appreciate the characters of the Arabic Alphabet)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: copy words and sentences accurately.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the characters of the Arabic Alphabet.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you develop a good handwriting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: copy words and sentences accurately.
5. Be able to: appreciate the characters of the Arabic Alphabet.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
